description:
Tidehaven — a small terraced town on a west-facing shore, a few decades from now, after people stopped throwing things away. Solar sails shade the market, cargo bikes do the work of vans, rainwater runs in open channels, and everything broken goes to the repair nook before it goes anywhere else. The tone is warm, ordinary and low-stakes: the drama here is a failing lamp, a late ferry, a disagreement about who left the roof beds unwatered. Not utopia — just a place that mends more than it buys.

Four places make up the town. Salt Quay is the landing on the shore where the ferry ties up twice a day. Market Terrace, one terrace above it, is where everyone ends up: stalls, the tea counter, the repair nook. The Terrace House on the second terrace is home to four of them. Wend Light stands far out on the headland, still lit by hand, about a forty-minute walk along the coast path — far enough that going there is a decision.

Language: English. Season and weather matter; the sea is always in earshot. This is the bundled demo world of Anima Verse and it stays safe for work — it exists to show the system working, so treat it as a real place to play in, not as a test harness.
